rules.rule_name: UI Rendering Frame Rate Optimization (60/120 FPS)
rules.explanation: Performing heavy computations, JSON parsing, or complex layout calculations on the main UI thread causes dropped frames and stuttering animations.
rules.do: Offload heavy computations, data parsing, and disk I/O to background isolates or worker threads, keeping the main UI thread strictly focused on rendering.
rules.dont: Do not execute blocking synchronous operations, large loops, or database queries directly on the main UI thread.

rules.rule_name: Efficient List Rendering and Lazy Loading (Virtualization)
rules.explanation: Rendering long lists by instantiating all item widgets simultaneously consumes excessive memory and causes severe scrolling lag.
rules.do: Use lazy-loading, virtualized list components (e.g., `ListView.builder` in Flutter, `FlatList` in React Native) that recycle views dynamically as the user scrolls.
rules.dont: Do not render entire long datasets or thousands of list items at once in a static, non-lazy container.

rules.rule_name: Optimized Asset Management and Image Caching
rules.explanation: Loading oversized raw images directly from network or disk without downsampling or caching exhausts device RAM and triggers out-of-memory crashes.
rules.do: Implement efficient image caching, automatic downsampling to target display dimensions, and modern compressed formats (e.g., WebP).
rules.dont: Do not load high-resolution raw images directly into memory without caching or compression layers.

rules.explanation: Passing excessive, rapid messages across the JavaScript-to-Native bridge in cross-platform frameworks introduces bottlenecks and latency.
rules.do: Batch bridge communications, cache native results locally, and minimize frequent cross-bridge method calls in performance-critical loops.
rules.dont: Do not make continuous, high-frequency synchronous calls across the platform bridge inside animation or gesture listeners.
